newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 21.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Greece today commemorates the 30th anniversary of the 1967 military dictatorship.

--The first organised response to the prospect of dialogue between Greece and Turkey has come from 32 ruling party PASOK MPs, who have sent a letter to Prime Minister Costas Simitis warning him that such a dialogue would be of benefit only to Ankara and that the only issue which should be on the agenda is the delineation of the Aegean continental shelf.

--While Greece continues to send troops to Albania to join the multinational protection force, Albanian underworld elements yesterday stole a coast guard vessel from under the noses of the Preveza coast guard.
--The 32 PASOK MPs said they would not support the government's moves towards dialogue with Turkey if it means dialogue on the gamut of issues on which the two countries differ.
--There's a problem now for Greece on how to retrieve the inflatable craft nicked by three Albanians yesterday. The craft is moored off the Albanian coast and guarded by heavily armed men.

--Leading PASOK cadres such as Ioannis Haralambopoulos, Anastasios Peponis and Stelios Papathemelis are among the 32 who have launched an attack on the government's moves towards dialogue with Turkey.
--Dimitra Liani-Papandreou, Andreas Papandreou's widow, is obsessed with politics, Justice Minister Evangelos Yiannopoulos says. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
